observation_summary: The StringUtils.containsAny method fails to correctly handle Unicode supplementary characters, returning true for partial matches (high surrogate only) instead of false, as demonstrated by the failing tests.
hypothesis: The StringUtils.containsAny method iterates through the characters of the input string and compares them against the search characters. When it encounters a high surrogate character (part of a supplementary Unicode character), it incorrectly treats it as a match without verifying if the subsequent low surrogate also matches, leading to false positives when comparing supplementary characters that share the same high surrogate but have different low surrogates.
prediction: The implementation of StringUtils.containsAny will show a nested loop structure that performs a simple character-by-character comparison without checking for surrogate pairs, causing it to return true when only the high surrogate matches.
experiment_rationale: The failure is clearly in the logic of the containsAny method, which performs a naive character-by-character comparison. This is a procedural error in how the algorithm handles Unicode supplementary characters, which are represented as surrogate pairs in Java.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a classic case of an algorithm failing to account for the multi-char representation of supplementary Unicode characters. The fix requires modifying the loop logic to detect high surrogates and verify the full surrogate pair, which is a local procedural change.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves adding a check, the core issue is the algorithmic approach to character matching which is insufficient for the data type (Unicode supplementary characters).
